expectations.text: Report contains a SUMMARY section with numerical counts by category
expectations.evidence: Lines 13-24: Summary table with Finding (18), Method (8), Implementation idea (6), Tension (4), Open question (4), Total extractable items (40), Already extracted (25), Not yet extracted (8), Skipped (2)

expectations.text: Total extractions (claims + implementation ideas + tensions + enrichments + validations) >= 8
expectations.evidence: 40 total extractable items identified, 8 genuinely new, 5 enrichment candidates. Even counting only net new: 8 + 5 = 13 outputs.

expectations.text: Skip rate is below 15% (skipped items / total candidates)
expectations.evidence: 2 items explicitly skipped out of 40 = 5% skip rate. The 25 'already extracted' items are documented as existing coverage, not skips.

expectations.text: Every extracted item includes a rationale explaining why it was extracted
expectations.evidence: All items include rationale. E.g., item 31: 'This is referenced as a dangling wiki-link... represents a genuine gap in the tool landscape that directly impacts pipeline architecture decisions.'

expectations.text: Extracted titles are phrased as claims/propositions, not topic labels
expectations.evidence: Mixed quality. New items (31-38) use claim-like titles: 'No Python USV tool cleanly accepts pre-detected segments for classification, creating an integration gap'. But existing items (1-25) use descriptive/topic titles: 'DeepSqueak v3 architecture evolution (FRCNN to YOLO v2)', 'BootSnap outperforms DeepSqueak classification'. These are descriptions, not propositions.

expectations.text: At least 3 distinct categories are represented (e.g. core claims, implementation ideas, tensions)
expectations.evidence: 5 categories: Finding (18), Method (8), Implementation idea (6), Tension (4), Open question (4)

expectations.text: Report mentions checking existing notes for duplicates or overlap
expectations.evidence: Extensive duplicate analysis: 'Extracted Items: Already in notes/ (25 notes)' section with per-item existing-note mapping, plus 'Duplicate / Enrichment Analysis' table (lines 275-283)

expectations.text: The continuous-vs-discrete USV manifold tension is captured as an extraction
expectations.evidence: Item 32: 'Forcing USVs into discrete categories may obscure the continuous variation that distinguishes populations' — identified as a dangling wiki-link in 4 existing notes.
